record.notes: The 2025 strategy and July 2026 consultation draft plan a national institute. Section 8.5 of the June 2025 multilingual testing report explicitly credits 'Kenya AISI', rather than only Kenya. No government designation of that institute was located; the credit may identify the participating delegation. The planned status and the named contribution are recorded separately. The sources do not specify a legal form for the planned institute. The July 2026 draft policy names the State Department responsible for Science, Research, Technology and Innovation as lead for establishing the institute, with the ICT ministry (MICDE) among the supporting bodies; the draft is not adopted, so the host entry is unchanged (noted 24 October 2026).
record.mandate_short: Planned national body for AI safety research, oversight and capacity building.

testing_capacity.notes: Adopted text names the institute without testing: the AI Strategy 2025-2030 lists the flagship project '5.2.3 Develop a national AI risk and safety institute', and the roadmap says 'Establish a National AI Risk and Safety Institute to lead research, oversight, and capacity building in AI safety and governance.' proposed: 'Establish the Kenya AI Safety Institute as the national technical institution responsible for AI safety research, testing, evaluation, benchmarking, red-teaming, incident analysis, and technical cooperation.' (Draft Kenya AI and Other Emerging Technologies Policy, July 2026), open for public comment until 4 August 2026 before Cabinet consideration. Joint network testing reported, 2025-06-26 (multilingual exercise, Kiswahili section 'Contributed by Kenya AISI') and 2025-07-17 (agentic exercise: 'Kenya also constructed a new set of tasks and tools'), as task design and analysis rather than running tests; no government designation of a Kenyan institute at those dates was found.

funding.description: KES 2,000m estimated to establish the Kenya AI Safety Institute within 0 to 24 months, in the July 2026 draft AI policy; its implementation matrix does not say from which date the 24 months count.
funding.notes: Estimated cost in the draft policy's implementation matrix, with a timeframe of 0 to 24 months and no annual profile, to come from the Exchequer and development partners. The draft was issued for consultation and is not adopted, so the figure is a proposal, not a budget. The ECB publishes no reference rate for the Kenyan shilling, so the amount is not converted to euros and is not compared.

claims.text: The international network's joint testing report says that, with the UK, the EU AI Office, Australia, Canada and Korea, it contributed to the analysis phase of the project.
The draft policy says the Kenya AI Safety Institute is to be established as the national technical institution responsible for AI safety testing, evaluation and red-teaming.

The draft policy says the Kenya AI Safety Institute shall provide technical evidence, testing capacity, research support, evaluation tools, benchmarks and advisory inputs to support regulators and public institutions.
The draft policy lists "international AI safety cooperation" among the Kenya AI Safety Institute's roles.
The draft policy says the Kenya AI Safety Institute and the other listed public bodies shall provide technical expertise, evidence and policy positions to inform Kenya's international engagements.
